When I saw £11,760 flash up on my screen, my hands were shaking so bad I nearly dropped my phone onto the kitchen floor. I bit my lip, shut my eyes, opened them again — the numbers were still there.

I’m Olivia, 36, from Birmingham. And where I’m from, miracles like this just don’t happen to people like me.

For the past six years, I’ve been working as a hotel cleaner in town. Three shifts a week, sometimes six — zero-hour contract, no proper sick pay, no room for error. Scrubbing other people’s loos, changing bedsheets, picking up dirty towels, and occasionally having a quiet cry in the mop cupboard when the shift got too brutal. My kids only ever saw me exhausted, stressed, and completely drained.

I’m a single mum raising two little ones — my boy’s 7 and my girl’s 10. My ex pays next to nothing in child support; it barely covers a basic school uniform from Asda. I honestly can’t remember the last time I bought something for myself. Even grabbing a Costa coffee on the way to work had become a luxury I couldn't afford.

Rent, sky-high gas and electric bills, credit card debt... taking out small payday loans just to cover the interest on previous ones. It was a vicious cycle. Every single month I’d sit down with a biro and a notepad and realise we were falling short again. The kids were eating beans on toast or buttered pasta three nights a week. I even ended up selling my gold earrings — the only thing my gran had left me — just to buy electricity vouchers.

One night, after a soul-destroying 14-hour shift, I was lying in bed unable to sleep. I was mindlessly scrolling through Facebook at 11pm just to switch my brain off, and I came across a post from this bloke. He was sitting in his van with a cup of tea, writing:

“Look, I’m no influencer. I’m just a normal brickie from Manny. But a couple of weeks back I gave BritishWin a go. Sounds mad, but I’ve made more on here than I do in a month on the building site. Didn't sell anything — just had a few spins on my phone and withdrew the cash straight to my card.”

He wasn’t shouting or trying to act big. Just showed a screenshot of a payout into his NatWest account, saying: “Put twenty quid in, it won’t break the bank.”

I thought to myself: “Sod it, what have I got to lose? I’m already skint.”

I tapped the link, downloaded BritishWin, and put £20 in — literally money I’d been saving for my boy’s new trainers for school.

The first couple of days, I played it super safe. Small wins here and there — £40, £70. I withdrew every single penny straight to my Barclays card. Just seeing actual money land in my account gave me a tiny glimmer of hope.

When that initial £20 ran out, I swore I wouldn't push my luck. But a few nights later, after an absolute nightmare shift — coming home with an agony in my back and tears in my eyes — I sat at the table and thought: “In for a penny, in for a pound. Things can't get any worse anyway.”

I deposited another £20 into BritishWin and gave the reels a spin.

At first, it was up and down — win a fiver, lose a fiver. But then the screen literally lit up in gold. The balance started ticking up right in front of my eyes: £1,200… £3,400… £5,800… £8,200… and finally stopped at £11,760.

I held my breath. I dropped my phone onto the table and sat there frozen, staring at my reflection in the dark glass. I refreshed the app, logged out, logged back in. The money was still there.

I walked into the kids' room, kissed my daughter on the forehead and whispered:
“Pack your bags, sweetie. We’re going down to Cornwall to see Gran for the weekend. We’ve got train fare and enough for a proper seaside break.”

She had no idea why I was crying, but I just held her tight. For the first time in years, I felt this massive, suffocating weight lift off my chest.

Within 48 hours, the payout hit my bank account. We paid off every single overdue energy bill. Cleared the debts. I took my boy straight to JD Sports and bought him proper brand-new Nikes. Paid for my daughter’s dance classes for a full year up front. And for the first time in my life, I bought myself a brand-new winter coat — not from a charity shop or Primark, but a proper quality coat from the high street.

I still log into BritishWin once a week for a quiet flutter. But now I do it relaxed, no stress, just a few quid for fun with a cup of tea in my hand.

And every time I walk past that hotel in town where I used to scrub toilets for minimum wage, I smile and think: “Who’d have thought a random Facebook post at 11pm could change our lives forever.”

I’m not telling anyone to go crazy. I’m just saying: sometimes, one little click really can change everything. xx

I’M GETTING THE HELL OUT OF THIS DAMN BRITAIN! 🇬🇧🤬

My name’s Sophie, I’m 34 years old, and I’m from Manchester.

All my life I’ve worked myself to the bone. First stacking shelves at Tesco for peanuts, then slogged away in construction and property renovations — painting, plastering, demolition, whatever came up. My hands are wrecked with calluses, my lower back is shot, and my wages were only ever enough to survive from one payday to the next.

My mum is the only family I’ve got left. She’s 64, and her health is failing. I have to buy her all the prescription meds and treatments that the NHS refuses to cover, drive her around, and manage the whole house on my own. Everything fell squarely on my shoulders.

I didn't have a life of my own.

No proper nights out down the pub, no holidays in the sun, no rest. Just pure, endless grind in the freezing rain.

Five years ago, out of sheer desperation, I started playing online slots now and then.

At first, it was just something to take my mind off the misery in the evenings after Mum went to bed. It gave me a bit of a buzz. Naturally, I got sucked in. Sometimes I’d win a few quid, but mostly I lost. But at least for twenty minutes, I felt human again.

Three weeks ago, a mate at work said to me:

“Sophie, have you seen that new app? Everyone’s talking about it — they’ve got massive welcome bonuses right now and the payout rates are way higher than usual.”

I just laughed it off at first.

But that evening, after looking at my mum’s tired face again, I thought:

“To hell with it. What have I got left to lose?”

I downloaded the app, set up an account, and deposited £25.

First few spins — dead. Nothing.

Later that evening, I added another £95 because I had this gut feeling that something was about to give.

The next day, during my tea break, I was testing a few classic slots and settled on one.

A couple of dry spins... and then BAM — Bonus Round.

A huge symbol dropped right across the reel...

And every single line lit up.

The screen flashed: **£38,450**.

I completely froze.

And then I just burst out screaming at the top of my lungs. Crying, laughing, jumping up and down in the kitchen.

Mum shouted from her room:

“Sophie, what on earth is going on?!”

I couldn’t even get the words out.

The biggest win I’d ever landed in five years was maybe £800.

And here I was staring at thirty-eight grand.

I left £450 on my balance and hit withdraw on **£38,000**.

Shortly after, the transfer was flagged as pending in my Barclays app for extra verification. I uploaded a quick screenshot of my withdrawal confirmation in the app, and within a couple of hours, the green light was given and the money dropped in. Every single penny.

I sat there and cried my eyes out — but this time, from pure relief.

I didn’t sleep a wink that night. I sat by Mum’s bed and realized: we’re done suffering in this freezing, miserable country.

A few weeks later, after sorting out Mum’s private health insurance and getting our papers in order, we flew out to Alicante, Spain. The warm Mediterranean climate is ten times better for her health than Manchester’s damp cold.

I rented a lovely two-bedroom flat in a quiet area and hired a local part-time carer for a few hours a day to sit with Mum while I’m out.

Since Brexit, getting a proper work visa is a nightmare, but I know how to work with my hands. I found cash-in-hand renovation gigs for British expats in two days flat.

Now I’m sitting on my sunny balcony, having a coffee, and you know what the crazy part is?

Using my UK SIM line in roaming, I logged back into the app the other day...

And I won again.

Two days ago — **£1,200**.

Straight into my account without any issues.

I sat there and cried again. Because for the first time in my adult life, I feel in control of my own future. My mum is warm and cared for, and I’m finally living.

I don’t know if I’ll ever move back to rainy Britain. Probably not.

If you’re sick of grinding yourself into the ground just to pay rent and bills — just give it a go.

I’ll drop the link to the exact app I used in the comments below.

Just put in £20 or £25 — whatever you’re fine losing — and don’t overthink it.

Maybe it’ll be your way out too.

Take care of yourselves. x

SQUEEZIE, SI TU LIS ÇA — VA TE FAIRE FOUTRE ! 🤬🖕 Si j'avais su dans quoi je m'embarquais à cause de ta promo...

Salut tout le monde. Pour ceux qui ne me connaissent pas : je m'appelle Camille, j'ai 31 ans, je suis caissière dans un Lidl à Creil et j'élève seule ma fille de 8 ans, Léa.

Pas de parents riches, pas de pension alimentaire de mon ex. Juste moi. Le loyer de notre petit T2 humide — où il y a de la moisissure sur les murs en hiver et où c'est un four en été — est passé à 720 € par mois. Mon salaire, même avec des heures sup', dépasse à peine les 1 400 € nets. Et quand la facture de régularisation EDF est tombée le mois dernier, j'ai failli m'évanouir. Une boule dans la gorge si forte que je n'arrivais plus à respirer.

Ces derniers temps, j'avais l'impression de devenir folle. Les horaires décalés, 8h debout par jour à scanner des articles pour des gens toujours pressés... Je rentrais tellement épuisée que je n'avais même plus la force de retirer mes baskets. La nuit, quand Léa s'endormait, je sortais sur le balcon glacé et je pleurais en silence. Pour ne pas qu'elle m'entende. Je demandais juste une chose : ne plus avoir à compter chaque centime. Ne plus ressentir cette angoisse paralysante au moment où le TPE met trop de temps à valider un paiement pour une baguette et du jambon... 😭

Le moment où j'ai craqué, c'était pour un truc bête. Léa est rentrée de l'école et m'a demandé timidement 85 € pour la sortie de classe au Parc Astérix. J'ai dû lui dire non. Je lui ai dit : « Peut-être la prochaine fois, ma puce », elle a juste baissé les yeux, murmuré : « D'accord maman » et elle est partie dans sa chambre.

Cette nuit-là, j'ai hurlé de pleurs dans la cuisine. Les semelles de ses bottes d'hiver se décollaient déjà, tenues par du scotch, et moi je n'avais même pas 85 pauvres euros pour que ma fille puisse partir avec ses copains. 💔

Le lendemain, pendant la pause déj, ma collègue Sarah m'a mis son téléphone sous le nez. « Camille, tu vas t'épuiser combien de temps encore pour des miettes ? », elle m'a dit.

Elle m'a montré une story de Squeezie. Dans la vidéo, Squeezie expliquait qu'il s'était associé à des développeurs pour sortir son application officielle, *Squeezie's Lucky Wheel*, pour donner une vraie chance aux gens de s'en sortir financièrement par les temps qui courent. Sarah m'a dit qu'elle avait testé pour rigoler et qu'elle avait sorti 900 € en un week-end ! Elle a ouvert son appli Revolut sous mes yeux et m'a montré les virements...

Je lui ai répondu direct : « Ouais, c'est ça, encore une arnaque TikTok ». Franchement, ça m'énervait. Mais cette idée m'a trotté dans la tête toute la journée.

Le soir, allongée dans mon lit, je défilais sur TikTok et Insta — cette pub était PARTOUT. Des gens vrais, des vidéos, des commentaires — tous disaient que Squeezie ne mentait pas et que les retraits arrivaient direct sur Revolut. Je me suis dit : et si j'étais juste une paranoïaque qui refuse la seule porte de sortie de cet enfer ?

J'ai téléchargé *Squeezie's Lucky Wheel* avant de changer d'avis. J'ai déposé mes derniers 10 € par Apple Pay — littéralement le fric qui devait nous nourrir jusqu'à vendredi. J'ai reçu direct le bonus de bienvenue : 255 tours gratuits + 200 € de bonus. Les mains me tremblaient. Je me sentais coupable. 😳

J'ai lancé la roue principale. Mon solde a commencé à grimper à une vitesse folle — 80 €, puis 400 €, puis 1 800 €... À un moment, c'est monté jusqu'à 3 200 € ! J'ai demandé un virement de 500 € pour tester. Quand une minute plus tard mon téléphone a vibré avec une notification Revolut confirmant la réception, j'ai bloqué : « Attends... c'est réel ?! »

Et puis j'ai fait l'erreur classique. L'avidité m'a attrapée, j'ai augmenté les mises. Mon solde s'est effondré jusqu'à tomber à 5 €. J'ai verrouillé mon téléphone et je suis restée dans le noir, à me détester : « Espèce d'idiote ! Tu as gâché tes derniers sous, bien fait pour toi ! »

Et je me suis rappelée qu'il me restait encore les 255 tours gratuits de Squeezie.

C'est là que ma vie a basculé. Un multiplicateur est tombé : x50... puis x100... et puis x2500 !!! L'écran a freeze une seconde avant de se remplir de pièces d'or. Je fixais les chiffres sans y croire. J'ai fermé et réouvert l'application dix fois, persuadée que c'était un bug d'affichage. 🔥

Sur mon solde, il y avait **184 500 €** !!! PRESQUE DEUX CENTS MILLE EUROS ! 🤯

Sur le coup, je n'ai ressenti aucune joie. Juste une PEUR PARALYSANTE. La peur que ce soit une erreur, que tout disparaisse. Les doigts tremblants, j'ai commencé à demander des retraits par tranches de 10 000 € sur mon compte Revolut.

Le lendemain matin, les premiers virements étaient déjà validés et les fonds arrivaient sans problème. Je tremblais de la tête aux pieds, mais quand j'ai vu ces chiffres grimper sur mon appli bancaire, j'ai juste posé ma tête sur la table de la cuisine et j'ai éclaté en sanglots. 😭

La première chose que j'ai faite était complètement irrationnelle. Au lieu de tout placer à la banque, j'ai posé une journée, j'ai récupéré Léa à l'école, on a pris le TER direction Paris et on est allées direct au Forum des Halles. Je lui ai acheté les bottes d'hiver les plus chères, une doudoune de marque qu'elle regardait toujours avec envie, et j'ai donné l'argent en liquide dans une enveloppe à sa maîtresse pour la sortie au Parc Astérix.

J'étais au milieu du centre commercial avec plein de sacs de marque, à pleurer comme une folle, pendant que ma petite fille sautait de joie dans ses nouvelles chaussures en me demandant inquiète pourquoi maman pleurait. 👟🎒

Maman ne pleure pas de tristesse, ma puce. Maman est juste heureuse pour la première fois depuis des années. ❤️

Et quant à toi, Squeezie... Cette nuit-là, quand je perdais, je t'ai insulté de tous les noms. Mais aujourd'hui... aujourd'hui je veux te dire MERCI de nous avoir sorties de cet enfer. 🙏

👇 UPDATE : Je reçois énormément de messages en privé pour me demander quelle est cette application. Je ne peux pas répondre à tout le monde, alors je laisse le lien officiel avec les 255 tours gratuits de Squeezie dans le premier commentaire épinglé ! Je vous souhaite autant de chance qu'à moi !

💔😢 33 YEARS OLD, SINGLE MUM IN LONDON. YESTERDAY I LEFT THE SUPERMARKET IN TEARS

My name is Laura Jansen, I’m 33 years old, and I’m raising my eight-year-old son Lucas on my own in Lewisham, London.

For those who don't live here: London is portrayed in the media as a city of pubs, red buses, and a glamorous lifestyle.

But my reality is completely different: alarm clock at six in the morning, endless waits for the bus and the Tube, and a retail worker wage from a clothes shop on Oxford Street that disappears before it even hits my bank account.

On £1,250 a month in London you don't live - you just try to survive.

Between rent that jumped to £820, Lucas’s school dinners, electric, gas, and £55 for an Oyster pass, the money evaporates in the first few days of the month.

I had just £25 left on my card for the rest of the month.

Everything became unbearable two months ago when I received a court letter through the post: a notice about a £5,200 bank debt that I had taken out just to cover living costs from previous months.

I lived in constant fear that my account would be frozen at any moment.

Last Tuesday, Lucas came home from school and showed me a flyer:

- Mum, my classmates are signing up for swimming lessons. It costs £120 with registration… can I go too?

I looked into his eyes full of hope - and then remembered that I had paid my last £150 towards the debt that morning. Remaining balance: £25.

I stroked his head and explained that it just wasn't going to work this month.

Lucas smiled sadly and said:

"Don't worry Mum, it’s alright, I didn't even like swimming that much anyway."

At just eight years old, he was already trying to protect me so I wouldn't feel bad.

That moment broke my heart into a thousand pieces.

The next day I went to the local supermarket to get something for tea.

At the till, when the bill came to £27.60, my card was declined: insufficient funds.

I was short by less than three pounds, but the transaction didn't go through.

People in the queue started sighing, shuffling their feet, and whispering impatiently.

I felt my face burning with embarrassment and everything started going blurry in front of my eyes.

I mumbled "sorry", left the shopping on the belt, walked outside, sat on the first bench I saw, and burst into tears.

"How did I get to this point? Working full-time, 40 hours a week, and I can’t even buy food for my son."

That night I couldn't sleep, going over that humiliation again and again in my head.

In a Facebook mums group, I saw a post by a girl.

She shared how she built a small emergency fund thanks to a phone app she played in her spare time.

At first I was skeptical and thought it was just another scam.

But looking at that £25 I had left, I said to myself:

"Things can't get much worse than this. £25 in London won't even last three days."

I downloaded the app, registered, and put £20 in from my card.

First three spins: nothing.

Balance dropped to £10.

I was ready to close it down when on the fifth spin the screen suddenly went dark.

A giant coin appeared and the word "BONUS" started flashing red.

My phone wouldn't stop vibrating.

The numbers on the screen started climbing like mad: £10 - £120 - £410 - £880… and stopped at £1,380.

I was in absolute shock.

My hands were shaking so much that I messed up entering my bank details three times.

At 02:15 AM I got a notification from my banking app: Transfer received £1,380.00.

I sat on the kitchen floor and cried.

For the first time in years, those were tears of pure relief.

I kept playing very carefully - only during my breaks and after Lucas went to sleep. Didn't buy anything extra. Everything I withdrew went towards bills, food, and absolute essentials for Lucas. I wasn't looking for a flashy lifestyle - I just wanted a chance to breathe out.

And then a week ago, something happened that made me write this and share it with everyone - I withdrew £6,500 from the app in one go.

What did I do first?

Immediately cleared that cursed bank debt of £5,200.

I bought Lucas new clothes, trainers, and swimming goggles, paid for the full swimming course at the pool, and filled the fridge to the top.

We still live in Lewisham, but the atmosphere at home is completely different.

Now I can look my son in the eyes and say: "Yes, darling, we can buy that," instead of: "Maybe next month, sweetie."

I’m not telling you this to promise you’ll get rich.

But if you’re a mum and feel like you just can’t cope with all this pressure anymore - sometimes you just have to give yourself a chance.

I’ll leave the link to the app in the first comment.

Have a look, if only for your own peace of mind.

“I WAS READY TO DELETE THE BLOODY APP… THEN THIS HAPPENED 😡”

My name’s Hannah, I’m 29 and I live in Leeds. I work as a care assistant, mostly doing long shifts, and quite often nights.

I’m nothing special. I don’t come from money, I don’t own a house and I definitely don’t have thousands sitting in savings. Like a lot of people, I work, pay my rent, sort out the bills and then try to make whatever’s left last until payday.

Recently it had all started getting on top of me.

Twelve-hour shifts, barely sleeping properly, constantly feeling tired and worrying about money. My car was getting old as well, and every time it made a new noise I’d think, “Brilliant… how much is this going to cost me now?”

There were nights when I’d get home after work, sit on the edge of my bed still wearing my uniform and just stare at the wall.

I didn’t want some millionaire lifestyle.

I just wanted to stop checking my bank account every time I went shopping and eventually get myself a decent car 🚗.

One night at work, one of the girls I was on shift with started talking about a new casino app she’d seen advertised on Facebook.

She was ridiculously excited about it and told us she’d already won £2,300.

I honestly thought she was winding us up.

She kept showing me screenshots of her wins and even showed me payments going into her bank account.

I laughed and said:

“Yeah, alright. And next week you’ll be buying a house in Spain.” 😂

She laughed as well, but kept telling me I should try it.

I didn’t think much more about it.

Then, a couple of days later, after another horrible night shift, I was sitting on the bus home scrolling through Facebook and the exact same advert appeared on my feed.

I ignored it.

Then it appeared again.

And again.

By that point I was actually getting annoyed 😤.

I remember thinking:

“Why does this bloody thing keep following me everywhere? What if she actually wasn’t talking rubbish and I’m just too scared to give it a go?”

When I finally got home it was nearly midnight. I made a cup of tea, got into bed and, for some reason, I was still thinking about what the girl at work had shown me.

Curiosity got the better of me.

I downloaded the app 📲, created an account and deposited £20.

Straight away I got a 100% bonus plus 250 free spins 🎁, so I had £40 on my balance.

I remember looking at it and thinking:

“Alright then… let’s see what happens.” 😏

I started playing 🎮.

I tried a few different games, but the ones I kept coming back to were Sweet Bonanza and Sugar Rush.

At first things were going surprisingly well.

My balance went from £40 to around £320.

I didn’t completely trust it, so I decided to withdraw £100 just to see whether the money would actually arrive.

When I saw it appear in my bank account, that was the moment I thought:

“Okay… this is actually real.” ✅

So I carried on playing from time to time after work.

And then came the bad evening.

Nothing was landing.

Every game I opened seemed completely dead.

Sometimes I was probably risking too much, and sometimes I was simply unlucky.

My balance kept dropping.

£150.

£80.

£30.

Eventually I looked at the screen and had just £4.80 left 😩.

I put my phone down and thought:

“For fuck’s sake. Why did I even bother?”

I genuinely nearly deleted the app there and then.

But then I remembered I still had some of the free spins left.

So I thought, screw it, I might as well use them.

That’s when things suddenly changed.

One bonus round landed.

Then another.

A x10 multiplier appeared.

Then another bonus.

I was sitting upright in bed watching the balance climb.

£120.

£260.

£500.

Eventually it reached around £980.

I honestly couldn’t believe it 😳.

After nearly wiping everything out, suddenly I was sitting there with almost a grand on the balance.

This time I decided not to be stupid.

I closed the app, put my phone down and went to sleep 😌.

The next day I deposited another £40, got another 100% bonus, and played carefully.

No rushing.

No chasing losses.

Mostly just games I already knew.

Some days were good.

Some were rubbish.

There were plenty of ups and downs.

But after about a week of playing, my balance had reached just over £5,400 😮.
